lines.japanese: 想像力の豊かな人間になりたいと思うんだ。
lines.english: I'd like to be someone with a rich imagination.

lines.japanese: たとえば朝、窓から射しこむ柔らかな陽の光にまぶたを撫でられて目を覚ます。
lines.english: For instance, I wake in the morning to soft sunlight streaming through the window, caressing my eyelids.

lines.japanese: ロココ調の家具に囲まれたベッドルームの窓辺に立ち、ネグリジェのままうんと伸びをする。
lines.english: I stand by the window of a bedroom furnished in the Rococo style and stretch luxuriously in my negligee.

lines.japanese: アーチ型の出窓を開けはなてば涼しい風がそよと頬を打ち、庭園の緑で羽をやすめる友人たちが心地よいさえずりで語りかけてくる。
lines.english: I throw open the arched bay window. A cool breeze brushes my cheeks, and my friends resting their wings in the garden greenery greet me with pleasant chirps.

lines.japanese: そうしたら私は柔和にほほえんで答えるんだ。
lines.english: Then I smile gently and answer them.

lines.japanese: おはよう小鳥さんたち、今日はとてもいい天気ね。
lines.english: Good morning, little birds. What lovely weather we're having.

lines.japanese: なんちゃって？　そんな風に、まあ、思ってみれば朝の目覚めもいくぶん快適になるんじゃないかと。
lines.english: Just kidding. But, well, imagining something like that might make waking up a little more pleasant.

lines.japanese: なあんて思ってはみるものの、まだまだ修行の足りない私は眠気と冬の朝の気温に克てず、そこまで手の込んだイマジネイションを展開することができないわけだ。
lines.english: Or so I tell myself. In practice, I still have a long way to go. Between the sleepiness and the cold of a winter morning, I'm in no condition to conjure up anything so elaborate.

lines.japanese: 縮こまる体に毛布を巻きつけたまま、愚図愚図と安物のベッドから下りる。
lines.english: Still huddled in my blanket, I drag myself out of my cheap bed.

lines.japanese: 結露だらけの窓の外では、週に二度のご馳走（燃えるゴミ）を食いちらかす住宅街のカラスがギャアギャアと鳴きわめいていた。
lines.english: Outside the condensation-covered window, the neighborhood crows squawk as they make a mess of their twice-weekly feast (the burnable trash).

lines.japanese: いい加減切ろうかとも思う長すぎる髪をわしゃわしゃ掻きまぜながら、私は寝起きのしわがれた声でつぶやく。
lines.english: I rumple the hair that's grown far too long—maybe it's time I cut it—and mutter in my hoarse, just-woke-up voice.

lines.japanese: 「……おはよう小鳥ども」
lines.english: “...Morning, you damn birds.”

lines.japanese: 拭えない眠気。遥かなるロココ。
lines.english: The sleepiness won't go away. Rococo is a distant dream.

lines.japanese: 想像力が足りないよね。
lines.english: Not enough imagination, huh?

lines.japanese: 窮屈なユニットにこもって、手っとり早くシャワーで眠気をすっとばしてきた。
lines.english: I shut myself in the cramped bathroom and blast the sleepiness away with a quick shower.

lines.japanese: 即物的だね。いいの、小鳥が鳴かないから。
lines.english: Very practical of me. That's fine. No birds singing in there.

lines.japanese: 下着姿のまま部屋を渡って、朝食代わりのビスケットをつまむ。
lines.english: I cross the room in my underwear and pick up a cookie to serve as breakfast.

lines.japanese: 環境音代わりのテレビでは、嫌味な胸の女子アナが今年のクリスマス商戦について、台本めいたコメントを挿しはさんでいた。
lines.english: On the TV I leave on for background noise, the announcer with the annoyingly big chest is making scripted-sounding remarks about this year's Christmas shopping season.

lines.japanese: 素敵ですねー、こんな指輪プレゼントされちゃったら、女性はみんなクラッと来ちゃいますよねー。
lines.english: How lovely! Any woman would just swoon if someone gave her a ring like this, wouldn't she?

lines.japanese: 「ないない、それはない」
lines.english: “Nope, nope. Not happening.”

lines.japanese: ひとり暮らしを始めてから安易な独り言が増えてしまった。しかも否定的な合いの手、つまりいちゃもんが多いのだ。
lines.english: Since I started living alone, I've fallen into the habit of talking to myself. Usually to butt in with something negative. In other words, to find fault.

lines.japanese: よくない傾向だね。否定は想像の妨げだよ。対義語にも等しい。
lines.english: Not a good trend. Negativity gets in the way of imagination. The two are practically opposites.

lines.japanese: 「それはない、そんなことはできない」という思考停止からの脱却──その最初の試みこそ、我々が想像と呼ぶものであろうトーマス君。
lines.english: The first attempt to break free of the mental dead end of ‘That's impossible, it can't be done’—surely that is what we call imagination, my dear Thomas.

lines.japanese: ちなみにトーマス君は電話やら映画やらの発明に大きく貢献したことで知られているけど、ガチで来世やら交霊やらの研究もしちゃっていたイマジネイション豊かすぎるおじさんだ。黒い噂もあるけど比較的ラブ。
lines.english: Incidentally, Thomas is known for his major contributions to inventions like the telephone and movies, but he also seriously researched things like the afterlife and communicating with spirits. The guy had a little too much imagination. There are some shady stories about him, but I kind of love him.

lines.japanese: 閑話休題。とりあえず、みだりに否定しない女になろう。そこから始めよう。うん、まあ、心がけ程度に。無理ならいいや。
lines.english: Anyway. For now, I'll try to be a girl who doesn't shoot everything down. Let's start there. Well, just something to keep in mind. If it doesn't work out, never mind.

lines.japanese: テレビに目を戻せば嫌味な胸の女子アナ、今度は高層階のしゃれたバーから見下ろす夜景に過剰な溜息。正直イラッとしつつも、私はさっそく否定しない練習。
lines.english: I look back at the TV. The announcer with the annoyingly big chest is now sighing far too much over the nighttime view from a stylish bar on a high floor. Frankly, it's getting on my nerves, but I get right to work on not being negative.

lines.japanese: 「へえ。いいかもねえ」
lines.english: “Huh. That might be nice.”

lines.japanese: こんなときこそ想像力なんだ。
lines.english: This is exactly when I need my imagination.

lines.japanese: クリスマスに浮かれる絶賛恋愛中の乙女たちを思うから鼻白んでしまう。
lines.english: It's thinking of all those lovestruck girls getting giddy over Christmas that puts me off.

lines.japanese: まずは自分がその場にいると思って、柔らかなキャンドルライトを思って、黄金色のアップルソーダを思って、そうしてから眼下に広がる街明かりの海を思ってみよう。
lines.english: First, picture myself there. Picture the soft candlelight. The golden apple soda. Then picture the sea of city lights spreading out below.

lines.japanese: 「ふむ……なるほど、素敵素敵」
lines.english: “Hmm... I see. Lovely, lovely.”

lines.japanese: 私は嫌味な胸の女子アナに追随した。あとは素敵な男性さえいれば～なんていう型どおりのオチにも、うんうんと共感する。いちおう私も乙女なのだ。なんちゃって。
lines.english: I go along with the announcer with the annoyingly big chest. I even nod sympathetically at her predictable conclusion: ‘Now, if only I had a wonderful man to share it with.’ I'm a girl too, after all. Just kidding.

lines.japanese: 二枚目のビスケットを拾いながら「なんちゃって」とは便利なフレーズだなあと思う。ひとこと文末に添えるだけで、たちまち照れくささも白々しさも厚かましさも緩和される。
lines.english: As I pick up a second cookie, I reflect on what a handy phrase ‘just kidding’ is. Tack it onto the end of a sentence, and the embarrassment, insincerity, or sheer nerve is instantly softened.

lines.japanese: 魔法の文字列だね。いつも心になんちゃってだね。メールだったら顔文字や（笑）でもいいね。
lines.english: Magic words. Always keep a ‘just kidding’ in your heart. In an email, a smiley or ‘lol’ will do too.

lines.japanese: おはよう小鳥さん。なんちゃって（笑）
lines.english: Good morning, little birds. Just kidding, lol.

lines.japanese: 「んむっ？」
lines.english: “Mmph?”

lines.japanese: くわえてたビスケットぱきり。
lines.english: The cookie between my teeth snaps in two.

lines.japanese: ベッドの上でタイツを穿こうとしたとき、電話が私を呼んだ。
lines.english: I'm sitting on the bed, about to pull on my tights, when the phone calls for me.

lines.japanese: 「誰だ、朝っぱらから」
lines.english: “Who's calling this early?”

lines.japanese: ケータイを開いて発信者名を確認する。母親だった。
lines.english: I flip open my cell phone and check the caller's name. My mother.

lines.japanese: 登校前の忙しいときに面倒だなあ。と思うものの、おっといかんね、否定から入っちゃいかん。私は一息吹いてから通話ボタンを押した。
lines.english: What a pain when I'm busy getting ready for school. But wait, no. Can't start by being negative. I let out a breath and press the answer button.

lines.japanese: 「はーい」
lines.english: “Hellooo.”

lines.japanese: 肉親向けのちょっと幼い声が出た。方言みたいなものだ。
lines.english: Out comes the slightly childish voice I use with family. It's like a dialect.

lines.japanese: 「おー明日香、おはよー」
lines.english: “Oh, Asuka. Morning.”

lines.japanese: 通話孔から返ってきたのは、アルコールの臭いが漏れてきそうな声。いいけど。彼女にとっては飲むのも仕事の一環だろう。
lines.english: The voice coming out of the earpiece sounds as though it could bring the smell of alcohol with it. That's fine. Drinking is probably part of her job.

lines.japanese: 私は若くして一人暮らしなんかしてるせいで、同年代の子と比べて、親によって生かされているという自覚がある方だと思う。
lines.english: Living on my own this young, I think I'm more aware than most kids my age of just how much I rely on my mother.

lines.japanese: 「うん、どうしたの？」
lines.english: “Yeah, what's up?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、べつにぃ？　どうしてっかなーと思って」
lines.english: “Mm, nothing? Just wondering how you're doing.”

lines.japanese: 急用でもないのに、わざわざ平日のこんな時間にかけてくるあたり、相変わらず自由なひとだ。
lines.english: Calling this early on a weekday when it's nothing urgent—she really does do whatever she feels like.

lines.japanese: 基本的には「超」が付くほど放任主義な親なんだけど、その反動か、無性に娘の声を聞きたくなる日がたまにあるみたいだ。
lines.english: As a parent, she's basically super hands-off. Maybe to make up for it, she has days when she just can't resist hearing her daughter's voice.

lines.japanese: 「どう、そっちは？　元気？」
lines.english: “How are things over there? Doing okay?”

lines.japanese: 「元気元気。ママは？」
lines.english: “Fine, fine. How about you, Mama?”

lines.japanese: ママとか、もうね、後ろに（笑）を付けたい。
lines.english: Mama. Honestly, I want to stick ‘lol’ after that.

lines.japanese: いい加減お母さんとか呼ぶようにしたいなあ、なんて思いはじめて早や十年。十年ですよ？　一度定着してしまった呼び方を変えるのは難しいね。
lines.english: It's been ten years since I first thought it was about time I started calling her Mom. Ten years, you know? Once a name sticks, it's hard to change it.

lines.japanese: いいや、人前じゃなきゃ。クラスの子にでも聞かれた日には、その場で自害するけども。
lines.english: Oh well, as long as it's not in public. If anyone from class ever heard me, I'd kill myself on the spot.

lines.japanese: はいマニフェスト。いつか私が子供をもうけたときには、最初からお母さんと呼ばせよう。キュウリが食べられなくても許してあげよう。毎日うんと抱きしめてあげよう。
lines.english: Right, here's my manifesto. If I ever have a child, I'll have them call me Mom from the start. I'll forgive them if they can't eat cucumbers. I'll give them lots of hugs every day.

lines.japanese: 「あんた、まだ期末テスト終わらないの？　たまにはこっちにも帰ってきなよ？」
lines.english: “Aren't your finals over yet? Come home once in a while, will you?”

lines.japanese: 母は母らしいことを言った。珍しい。しかしママ上どの、私が実家に帰ったところで、どのみち仕事の忙しいあなたとは会えないと思うのだが。
lines.english: My mother says something motherly. Unusual. But, honored Mama, even if I came home, I doubt I'd see you, busy with work as you are.

lines.japanese: 「ま、会えないんだけどさ！」
lines.english: “Well, I wouldn't get to see you anyway!”

lines.japanese: 自分で言った。
lines.english: She said it herself.

lines.japanese: 母は私を産んだだけあって、私と同じく、なんちゃって症候群だった。
lines.english: As you'd expect from the woman who gave birth to me, my mother has just-kidding syndrome too.

lines.japanese: つまり真面目なこと・お行儀よいことを言ったあとには「なーんちゃって」に相当するオチを付けて、きんと冷えた空気を中和させねば気が済まない性質なのだ。たとえば──
lines.english: Meaning, after she says something serious or properly behaved, she has to add some version of ‘Juuust kidding’ to take the chill out of the air. For instance—

lines.japanese: 私はそんな母が大好きです（←まじめ）
lines.english: I love my mother just as she is. (← serious)

lines.japanese: 平均より多めの小遣いくれるしね（←おどけ）
lines.english: She gives me more spending money than most people get, too. (← kidding around)

lines.japanese: 「ちゃんと栄養とってんの？　野菜食べてる？　億劫がって自炊してないんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Are you eating right? Getting your vegetables? I bet you're not cooking because you can't be bothered.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、米のとぎ方すら忘れてるひとに言われたくないよ。ママこそちゃんとしなー？」
lines.english: “Ha ha, I don't want to hear that from someone who's forgotten how to rinse rice. You're the one who needs to take care of herself, Mama.”

lines.japanese: 「もう……お義姉さんのご近所ってことだから、一人暮らしを許したんだけどねぇ。あのひと、ちゃんとおまえの面倒みてくれてんの？」
lines.english: “Honestly... I only let you live alone because you'd be near your aunt. Is she actually looking after you?”

lines.japanese: 「まー、伯母さんもママに輪をかけて放任主義だからね。でも大丈夫だよ、適度に保護者してもらってる」
lines.english: “Well, Auntie's even more hands-off than you. But it's okay. She's doing enough of the guardian thing.”

lines.japanese: 「そーお？　ならいいけど……」
lines.english: “Is she? Well, all right, then...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、心配してくれてありがと」
lines.english: “Yeah. Thanks for worrying about me.”

lines.japanese: なんだこりゃ。おままごとみたいな会話。ほほほ、愉快愉快。
lines.english: What is this? It's like we're playing house. Ho ho ho, how delightful.

lines.japanese: なんて優雅な朝を過ごせるほどには早起きしていない。
lines.english: Except I haven't gotten up early enough to enjoy such a leisurely morning.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんママ、私そろそろ出なきゃ。電話代ももったいないしさ」
lines.english: “Sorry, Mama, I have to get going. No point running up the phone bill, either.”

lines.japanese: 「あ。そうだ明日香！　あんた先月の電話代、何アレ使いすぎ！」
lines.english: “Oh, that reminds me, Asuka! What was that phone bill last month? You used it way too much!”

lines.japanese: しまった、ヤブヘビ。
lines.english: Damn. Should've let sleeping dogs lie.

lines.japanese: 先月っていうとアレか。島本の彼氏がバイト先の女と致しただか致しかけただかで、あいつの愚痴と泣き言に三時間以上付きあわされたアレだ。
lines.english: Last month? Oh, that. Shimamoto's boyfriend did, or almost did, the deed with some woman at his part-time job, and I had to listen to her complaining and crying for over three hours.

lines.japanese: や、アレはねえ、だって、数学といえばシマモトさんでお馴染みの島本でしょ。あの子には日ごろ何かと世話になってるし、今後とも末永く懇意にしていただきたいわけだし、ねえ？
lines.english: Well, come on. This is Shimamoto, the very same Shimamoto renowned for being the person to ask about math. She helps me with all kinds of things, and I'd very much like to remain on good terms with her for years to come, you know?

lines.japanese: 「明日香のことだから、好き好んで長電話したわけじゃないとは思うけど」
lines.english: “Knowing you, Asuka, I doubt you were talking that long because you wanted to.”
“Well...”

lines.japanese: 「あんた私に似て、根は暗いくせして八方美人だからねえ」
lines.english: “You're like me. Gloomy underneath it all, but you still try to please everyone.”
“Yeah...”

lines.japanese: 返す言葉もない。そういうとこは見透かされてるのか。このひとは分かってるんだか分かってないんだか。
lines.english: I have nothing to say to that. So she sees through that part of me. Does this woman understand me or doesn't she?

lines.japanese: 「寂しい思いさせちゃってる私も悪いんだけどさあ」
lines.english: “It's partly my fault for leaving you lonely, though.”

lines.japanese: あれ、やっぱり分かってないのか。
lines.english: Oh. So maybe she doesn't.

lines.japanese: あのねママ上、あなたがいなくて寂しいだなんて可愛らしい我がままを言っていたのは、私がまだキュウリを食べられなかった遥か昔の話だよ。
lines.english: Listen, honored Mama. It's been a very long time since I made those cute little selfish complaints about being lonely without you. Back when I still couldn't eat cucumbers.

lines.japanese: 妹や弟が欲しいだなんて泣きついて、その場にいた微妙な容姿の常連さんをその気にさせてしまい、あなたを二重の意味で困らせたのは、私が子どもの作り方を知らなかった遥か昔の話だよ。
lines.english: And it's been a very long time since I cried for a little sister or brother, gave an iffy-looking regular who happened to be there ideas, and embarrassed you in two different ways. Back when I didn't know how babies were made.

lines.japanese: そんな無茶はとうに引っこみ、いまではあなたの働きぶりに感謝することしきりです。
lines.english: I've long since stopped making impossible demands like that. These days, I'm nothing but grateful for all the work you do.

lines.japanese: あなたが職場で身を削っているおかげで、私の衣食住は確保されている。ひとりで気ままな朝を迎えられるのも、そよ風や小鳥さんにおはようを言えるのも、みんなあなたのおかげなのですから。
lines.english: It's because you wear yourself down at work that I have food, clothes, and a roof over my head. That I can spend my mornings alone as I please, saying good morning to breezes and little birds. It's all thanks to you.

lines.japanese: 「あ、やばっ。遅刻しちゃうから切るね。ばいばい」
lines.english: “Oh, crap. I'm gonna be late, so I have to hang up. Bye.”

lines.japanese: だけど根が暗い私は、とくに母を誉めることも慰めることもせず問答無用で電話を切った。
lines.english: But I'm gloomy at heart, so I cut the call short without a word of praise or comfort for my mother.

lines.japanese: キュウリが食べられなかったころに抱えていた孤独ぶんぐらいの、これはささやかな復讐なのだ。
lines.english: A small revenge, worth about as much as the loneliness I carried back when I couldn't eat cucumbers.

lines.japanese: うそうそ。ほんとに遅刻しそうなの。
lines.english: Kidding, kidding. I really am about to be late.

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: 慌ただしく部屋を出て、マンションの階段を駆けおりている最中に気付いた。
lines.english: I hurry out of my apartment and am halfway down the stairs when I realize.

lines.japanese: 「ちゃー、財布──」
lines.english: “Agh, my wallet—”

lines.japanese: ──を忘れた。
lines.english: —I forgot it.

lines.japanese: 階段のなかばで立ちどまり、一瞬悩んだ。どうしよう。すでに遅刻ぎりぎりの時間、さて取りに戻るか戻らざるや。
lines.english: I stop in the middle of the stairs and hesitate. What do I do? There's barely enough time to make it to school. To go back or not to go back?

lines.japanese: 「ま、いっか」
lines.english: “Oh well.”

lines.japanese: べつにね。一日ぐらいね。帰りに寄り道とかしなければね。
lines.english: It's fine. Just one day. As long as I don't stop anywhere on the way home.

lines.japanese: だって、学校の敷地内でお金の使いどころなんて、せいぜい学食ぐらいしかないでしょ？
lines.english: After all, the only place I'd spend money at school is the cafeteria, right?

lines.japanese: そーんな、全然！　全然、全然。ねえ？　一食ぐらいなんて、抜いたって大したことないない。むしろダイエット感覚だよね。
lines.english: Oh, it's nothing! Nothing, nothing. Right? Missing one meal is no big deal. If anything, it's like going on a diet.

lines.japanese: や、実はね、ここだけの話だがね、どうもこのところ、この辺にこう……付いておるのだよ、ぷに然とした肉が。
lines.english: Actually, between you and me, lately I've been acquiring a little... flesh around here. The squishy sort.

lines.japanese: そりゃ人前じゃあ涼しい顔して「エー私食べてもぜんぜん肥えないだけだしー」なんて見栄張っちゃいますがね、わりとひそかに努力もしてるんですよ。
lines.english: Sure, in public I'll put on a cool face and say, ‘Oh, I just never gain weight, no matter how much I eat.’ But I do put in a fair amount of effort in secret.

lines.japanese: ほら、いつ素敵な男性が指輪を持って現れるか分からないしね。私もいちおう乙女なのだ。なんちゃ（略）
lines.english: You never know when a wonderful man might turn up with a ring, you know. I'm a girl too, after all. Just kid—(etc.)
